title: Zephyr: frame parse/serialize
description: Frame parsing and serialization in Zephyr. DONE - link/frame.c
notes:
2026-08-27 full current-spec read-only audit: modern canonical signed corpus test/vectors/link_frame_signed_modes.json contains six positive modes/boundaries with LLSec a6/a3/a0/a5/a2/a7, required 8-byte signer EUI-64 after destination, and signed maximum payloads. Current Zephyr frame.c rejects all six immediately because bit7 is declared reserved; writer emits only bit5, rejects any signer field, and sizes payload without the signer octets. It also accepts noncanonical S-only frames instead of enforcing S==SI. Existing host frame test binary passed 16/16, including unsigned bounds/encryption/NULL cases, but its so-called canonical signed tests hard-code stale 0x20/0x21 frames and explicitly assert signer_iid_present=false, so it cannot satisfy the modern positive/negative corpus. Shared frame sources/tests remain read-only due concurrent work. Added exact blocker project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.1.5.4.3; no additional Schnorr dependency is needed because Zephyr deterministic sign/verify implementation beads .1.9.2.3/.1.9.3.3 are already closed. Acceptance remains open until C parses/writes SIID, enforces S==SI, accounts for signer bytes at all max-size boundaries, and consumes the shared positive/malformed vectors.
Completed the current canonical Zephyr frame codec. Parsing now builds a zeroed candidate and publishes only after complete validation, so every failure leaves caller state unchanged; serialization validates NULL payload, size, flag, address, signer, MIC, and buffer failures before touching output. Added a deterministic build-time C corpus generated directly from all 14 link_frame.json and all 6 link_frame_signed_modes.json vectors. Focused C now checks all four address modes, both MIC selectors, S/SI, unsupported E, all selectors 2-7, exact SIID/DST/payload/MIC layout, every proper truncation, trailing bytes, 255/256-byte boundaries, byte-exact reserialization, and failure atomicity. SCHC fragment fields are intentionally inside the opaque authenticated 0x14 payload under the current frame spec; no separate outer-frame fragment fields exist or were invented. Validation: strict host C passed 18/18 with explicit ASan+UBSan; cppcheck C23 and diff check passed; Python frame/vector parity passed 135 with 10 expected skips and ruff passed; Rust base corpus passed 14 vectors and Schnorr signed-mode corpus passed; local Zephyr 4.1 qemu_x86 link_crypto GCC12/-std=c2x build and runtime passed 18/18. No shared link.h, Python, Rust, or vector files modified.
close_reason: Canonical bounded frame parse/serialize and parity validation complete
